state_summary: Round 6, seed 157, free_llm32_dual_expert_v1: the packet reports 525 observed records, 2,805 eligible candidates and no pending experiments. The supplied tables support conditional loading responses, heterogeneous structural transfer and delayed ratio transitions. Recent measurements resolve several previous questions and reduce the value of routine expansion in established neighborhoods. Overall retrained Row accuracy and label-efficiency gains remain unverified.

important_observations.statement: H9 is narrowed: at 5/1, m173 V2 is 61.87 ml with DCM 1,500 ul (1e971da91b3a8229f0e0) and 60.92 ml with 2,000 ul (1e775e7d8dcbf48fd6f8). The larger plug does not preserve the large positive V2 shift seen at 0/1 and 1/1. Also, the 1,500 ul curve rebounds from 46.22 at 2/1 to 61.87 at 5/1; the earlier description of a continuing post-1/1 decline was too broad. Further routine m173 expansion has diminished value.

H10 is supported with corrected loading alignment. At 150 ul, m13 V1/V2 are 9.04/18.17 at 2/1, 17.85/43.86 at 5/1 and 36.93/94.21 at 10/1 (2dbfdf9c2d5defd09f7a, 5d530b2f228ed39ff952, ca467c94f14b2219503e). At 5/1, the 50 ul record is 23.90/40.10 (1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23): increasing sample volume advances V1 by 6.05 ml while delaying V2 by 3.76 ml. The older 10/1 record 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b uses 100 ul.

important_observations.statement: m199 rejects the previous saturation expectation. At fixed 150 ul, V1/V2 increase from 27.42/52.38 at 5/1 to 57.86/114.60 at 10/1 (6bd128bde2e137ea54f3, aa83ae83c0fa0cc37777). The 10/1 acquisition prediction underestimated V2 by 60.47 ml. Conversely, the measured 5/1 V2 values at 100 and 150 ul differ by only 0.08 ml. Missing high-ratio behavior has greater diagnostic value here than another routine 5/1 loading point.

H2 remains local. For m19 at 2/1, increasing sample volume from 50 to 150 ul changes V1 from 23.69 to 13.39 ml while V2 remains 34.83 to 35.04 ml (6d21e9ec887b3408c612, 906bd247e050658f99d8). For m212 at 5/1, increasing volume from 50 to 100 ul instead increases both endpoints from 7.24/13.67 to 22.07/37.18 (d5234e966aa231be05e5, 252c027cf5a42b92c953). A universal loading direction is contradicted.

The actual m205 1/1 loading corner is now measured. V1/V2 are 10.51/25.36, 18.27/33.28 and 16.77/34.09 at 50, 100 and 150 ul (b1fcf9bf2e03028d2ef8, 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8, 1aceeb0ee0419209d1c7). Most V2 change occurs between 50 and 100 ul. At 2/1, the 100-to-150 ul change is only -1.57/-0.51 ml (c973d4c257be9ef08216, 91b6bda771851a5c78ac). The response is ratio dependent rather than a constant amount offset.

important_observations.statement: H3 gains specific support from failed alcohol transfer: at 5/1 and 100 ul, m119 measures 48.00/77.09 versus m120 14.67/19.14 ml (776ee2c1e85ebde75168, e4fd83fb3852eb354a66). Their historical V2 errors have opposite signs, -34.20 and +34.37 ml. Nominal sample and solvent-volume conditions match, although density and loading mass differ. m80 also remains near 7.31 ml V2 at both measured 1/1 and 5/1, weakening broad transfer of the m13 tail; its loading solvent differs from m13.

New condition pairs reveal different slopes: m36 rises from 11.37/21.32 at 1/1 to 22.32/39.86 at 2/1 (efe7c6b0783a33974807, 6b7209c2e8154837a8c7), while m64 changes only from 5.72/9.66 at 2/1 to 5.93/11.06 at 5/1 (da91e1af5bac578c9384, 9449e3a7076ce90324ad). m28 V2 increases from 25.12 to 38.69 between 2/1 and 5/1, with relatively modest V1 movement (5522a1ec1f8e39cedb13, bfbe491a54086b98874d). These constrain slopes as well as molecular offsets.

H7's loading-reversal interpretation is weakened. Exact m92 20/1, 100 ul repeats measure V2 29.625 and 33.317 ml (8b58e9d7a710f55e49d3, bbb514661c0a49694d6a), a 3.69 ml difference. The latest repeat is only 1.23 ml below the 50 ul anchor of 34.55 (66da447ca0fe7160cc1c). The broader ratio-dependent tail remains supported; repeated-input variability can explain much of the apparent loading reversal.

H5's completed m125 1/1 surface remains supported: increasing DCM from 300 to 500 ul delays V2 by approximately 18–19 ml across measured sample volumes. Its 2/1 V1 valley remains unreplicated. Established m167 interpolation has also been accurate in recent acquisitions. Neither neighborhood warrants routine expansion without a remaining discriminating question.

important_model_behaviors.statement: Several candidate predictions remain nearly invariant across sample volume despite large measured loading effects. For example, m19 at 2/1 and 100 ul predicts 18.97/34.49 ml, whereas measured 50 and 150 ul V1 differ by 10.30 ml. An intermediate label can test response shape even when uncertainty or novelty is low.

Quantile outputs have structural problems. V1 q10 is zero in the displayed candidate records, making V1 quantile width closely tied to predicted endpoint scale. Some q50 values exceed q90 or fall below q10. Current m62 candidate cb79e57eb461a7dcc59a also predicts V1/V2 5.06/4.57. These are model-output defects, not measured chromatographic anomalies. The original H4 acquisition premise remains rejected by the ordered measured m13 and m80 endpoints.

Historical error signs vary across related molecules and conditions. Tail underprediction and excessive transfer both occur. A blanket upward V2 correction, common polar-group offset or forced global monotonic response would conflict with measured feedback.

possible_learning_bottlenecks: Delayed transitions remain incompletely located, especially in newer m199, m191 and alcohol neighborhoods. Labels that distinguish molecular offsets from ratio-dependent slopes may improve transfer more than isolated extremes.

Loading interactions affect endpoints differently. A shared representation with endpoint-specific interactions is an ML prior worth considering; its superiority over the current QGeoGNN treatment is untested.
Some substantial V1 structure is hidden by a focus on V2 tails. m19, m107 and m216 suggest amount-sensitive onset with comparatively stable completion.

Historical acquisition residuals are adaptively concentrated and were generated by successive models. They identify past local failures but cannot quantify current overall Row error or acquisition benefit.

Repeated inputs demonstrate variability, but a universal noise floor is unsupported. Large condition differences should not automatically be attributed to noise, and small differences should not automatically be encoded as deterministic interactions.
coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: The supplied pool spans ordinary low-to-moderate responses, steep tails and chemically unobserved molecules. Dense prior attention to m125, m167, m92, m173 and several polar tails should not crowd out representative structural coverage.

Distinct IDs can have identical molecule and condition inputs. Examples include m75 dccd8753d89546cbf994 and ef8724fc040ffeca44b7, and m69 3584971523a9f99cac5c and 686cce1ee0199615cff5. Deduplicate by the full input tuple when assessing redundancy; retain repeats only for a stated variability question.

Chemical similarity of 1.0 usually reflects an already observed molecule, not coverage of its entire condition surface. Conversely, high similarity below 1.0 can still expose a structural transfer failure.

m199 at 5/1 is already anchored at 100 and 150 ul. Its eligible 50 ul candidate f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c now has lower marginal value than the previous memo suggested unless resolving low-volume behavior is specifically important.

particularly_informative_candidates.reason: m212, 5/1, 150 ul, PE 300 ul; predicts 17.07/29.54 ml. Complements the measured large 50-to-100 ul change and distinguishes continuation, saturation or a localized amount interaction.
m19, 2/1, 100 ul, DCM 300 ul; predicts 18.97/34.49 ml. Tests interpolation across the measured 10.30 ml V1 loading change with almost stable V2.

m37, 5/1, 100 ul, DCM 400 ul; predicts 12.78/28.07 ml. This is a genuine ratio gap: the stored purported m37 5/1 observation e2f15590b7142490599b is actually m92. Connects measured m37 2/1 and 20/1 at 100 ul.
m28, 10/1, 100 ul, DCM 300 ul; predicts 26.08/62.45 ml. Extends the measured fixed-input 2/1-to-5/1 slope and tests further growth after V2-specific underprediction.

m191, 5/1, 50 ul, DCM 400 ul; predicts 9.08/27.70 ml. Could locate the missing intermediate regime, but comparison with measured 100 ul anchors changes both ratio and amount; an offset interpretation would remain confounded.
m115, 10/1, 100 ul, DCM 300 ul; predicts 15.23/32.70 ml. Tests near-saturation versus continued growth after its measured 5/1 result of 13.98/30.66 ml.

m13, 5/1, 100 ul, DCM 300 ul; predicts 19.03/38.40 ml. Tests loading interpolation and a predicted V2 dip below both measured 50 and 150 ul values. Its value is narrower now that the delayed tail is established.
Unobserved m30, 1/1, 100 ul, DCM 300 ul; predicts 5.25/10.73 ml. Adds an ordinary aryl-ketone transfer case alongside measured haloaryl and methoxy ketones, without requiring a tail assumption.

Unobserved m40, 0/1, 50 ul, DCM 300 ul; predicts 4.55/9.62 ml. Provides fused-aromatic ketone coverage at a common low-response condition; complementary ratio candidates exist, so its usefulness depends on an interpretable transfer question.

Unobserved m179, 1/1, 100 ul, DCM 300 ul; predicts 4.61/12.01 ml. A high-similarity structural comparison with measured cyclic ketone m180 at matching nominal conditions can test whether the representation distinguishes ring-size effects.

warnings: Only observed-table IDs establish measured evidence. Candidate values above are predictions, not future labels or expected errors.
Sample volume, loading mass and density are coupled; loading-solvent identity and volume are separate inputs. Apparent condition effects do not by themselves establish a chemical mechanism.
Higher PE/EA is PE-richer and generally weaker on silica; 0/1 is pure EA. Measured local exceptions prevent imposing a universal endpoint trend.
V2 minus V1 is an elution interval, not uncertainty. Quantile width, novelty and similarity have no demonstrated calibration as acquisition value.

Earlier advisory summaries contain mapping and residual-interpretation errors. The supplied observed rows take precedence, including the m13 loading correction and the m92 versus m37 identity correction.
